title: Placement Quest
bigIdea: A quick check-in so we know where to start you. There is no pass or fail.

cards.title: Show us what you know
cards.body: This is a quick check-in, not a test. Answer however you like. We will use it to pick the best place for you to start.

cards.title: No pass or fail
cards.body: Nothing here is graded and no answers are marked right or wrong. Just go with your gut and keep moving.

steps.prompt: You put $100 in a savings account that earns interest. What does "interest" mean here?

options.text: Extra money the bank pays you for keeping your money there
A fee you pay the bank each month

steps.explanation: Interest is money a bank pays you for holding your deposit.

steps.prompt: A budget is a plan for your money. What is it mostly used for?

options.text: Deciding how much to spend and save ahead of time
Making your money grow by itself

steps.explanation: A budget plans your spending and saving before the money is spent.

steps.prompt: Inflation means that, over time, the same amount of money usually buys a little less.
steps.explanation: Inflation is the slow rise in prices, so a dollar buys less over time.

steps.prompt: What is a "share" of a company?

options.text: A small slice of ownership in that company
A loan the company must pay back to you
A coupon for the company's products

steps.explanation: A share is a small piece of ownership in a company.

steps.prompt: A stock exchange is best described as...

options.text: A marketplace where people buy and sell shares
A bank that stores your cash
A government office that prints money

steps.explanation: A stock exchange is a marketplace for buying and selling shares.

steps.prompt: If a company's stock price goes up after you buy, your shares are worth more than you paid.
steps.explanation: A higher price means each share you own is worth more than your purchase price.

steps.prompt: In investing, what does "risk" usually refer to?

options.text: The chance that an investment loses value
A promise that you will earn money
The fee charged to open an account

steps.explanation: Risk is the chance an investment loses value.

steps.prompt: Why do people spread money across several investments instead of just one? (This idea is called diversification.)

options.text: So one bad investment hurts them less

steps.explanation: Spreading money out (diversification) softens the blow if one investment drops.

steps.prompt: An investment that could earn a lot usually comes with a higher chance of losing money too.
steps.explanation: Higher possible reward almost always comes with higher risk.

steps.prompt: Sort each item into where it belongs.

items.text: Cash in an insured savings account

steps.explanation: Insured cash savings is usually lower risk; a single new company's stock is usually higher risk.
